quotes.text: If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.security_relevance: Know the environment and the adversary model before acting.
quotes.source_reference: The Art of War, Lionel Giles public-domain translation, Chapter 3
quotes.translation_note: English public-domain translation; wording varies by translator.

quotes.text: The supreme art of war is to subdue the enemy without fighting.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.security_relevance: Prefer prevention, hardening, and containment over dramatic response.
quotes.source_reference: The Art of War, Lionel Giles public-domain translation, Chapter 3
quotes.translation_note: English public-domain translation; wording varies by translator.

quotes.text: All warfare is based on deception.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.security_relevance: Treat appearances as evidence to test, not conclusions to trust.
quotes.source_reference: The Art of War, Lionel Giles public-domain translation, Chapter 1
quotes.translation_note: English public-domain translation; wording varies by translator.

quotes.text: He will win who knows when to fight and when not to fight.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu
quotes.security_relevance: Response timing matters; not every signal requires disruptive action.
quotes.source_reference: The Art of War, Lionel Giles public-domain translation, Chapter 3
quotes.translation_note: English public-domain translation; wording varies by translator.

quotes.text: Do nothing which is of no use.
quotes.author: Miyamoto Musashi
quotes.security_relevance: Avoid noisy actions that do not improve evidence, containment, or resilience.
quotes.source_reference: The Book of Five Rings, commonly rendered precept
quotes.translation_note: Short English rendering; translations vary.

quotes.text: War is the realm of uncertainty.
quotes.author: Carl von Clausewitz
quotes.security_relevance: Security decisions often happen with incomplete evidence and must be revisable.
quotes.source_reference: On War, public-domain English translations
quotes.translation_note: Short passage from public-domain translations; wording varies.

quotes.text: Let him who desires peace prepare for war.
quotes.author: Vegetius
quotes.security_relevance: Prepared controls and recovery plans reduce panic during incidents.
quotes.source_reference: Epitoma Rei Militaris, maxim traditionally rendered as Si vis pacem, para bellum
quotes.translation_note: Traditional English rendering of Latin maxim.

quotes.text: The bravest are surely those who have the clearest vision of what is before them.
quotes.author: Thucydides
quotes.security_relevance: Clear evidence and sober assessment support better response decisions.
quotes.source_reference: History of the Peloponnesian War, public-domain English translations
quotes.translation_note: English public-domain translation; wording varies by translator.

quotes.text: Before you start some work, always ask yourself three questions.
quotes.author: Chanakya / Kautilya
quotes.security_relevance: Pause to define purpose, impact, and validation before changing systems.
quotes.source_reference: Chanakya Niti tradition; common short maxim requiring translation caution
quotes.translation_note: Traditional attribution; wording varies across collections and translations.

quotes.text: You have power over your mind, not outside events.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.security_relevance: Stay calm and control the response process when signals are noisy.
quotes.source_reference: Meditations, public-domain English translations
quotes.translation_note: English public-domain translation; wording varies.

quotes.text: It is not things that disturb us, but our judgments about things.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.security_relevance: Separate observed evidence from interpretation before escalating.
quotes.source_reference: Enchiridion, public-domain English translations
quotes.translation_note: English public-domain translation; wording varies.

quotes.text: Luck is what happens when preparation meets opportunity.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.security_relevance: Good incident outcomes often come from preparation done before the event.
quotes.source_reference: Commonly attributed to Seneca; exact source disputed
quotes.translation_note: Disabled by default because attribution is disputed.

quotes.text: Those who would give up essential Liberty, to purchase a little temporary Safety, deserve neither Liberty nor Safety.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.security_relevance: Security controls should be transparent, proportionate, and accountable.
quotes.source_reference: Pennsylvania Assembly reply, 1755

quotes.text: Public sentiment is everything.
quotes.author: Abraham Lincoln
quotes.security_relevance: Security programs need trust, clarity, and accountable communication.
quotes.source_reference: Lincoln-Douglas debate, 1858

quotes.text: Build a bridge before you need to cross the river.
quotes.author: Proverb
quotes.security_relevance: Prepare backups, access paths, and recovery evidence before incidents.
quotes.source_reference: Traditional proverb; no single author
quotes.translation_note: Proverb wording varies by collection.

quotes.text: Trust in God, but tie your camel.
quotes.author: Proverb
quotes.security_relevance: Trust does not replace verification, controls, and evidence.
quotes.source_reference: Traditional Arabic proverb; no single author
quotes.translation_note: Proverb wording varies by collection.

quotes.text: Forewarned is forearmed.
quotes.author: Proverb
quotes.security_relevance: Early warning has value only when it leads to readiness.
quotes.source_reference: Traditional proverb; Latin antecedent praemonitus praemunitus
quotes.translation_note: Traditional English rendering.

quotes.text: Dripping water can penetrate stone.
quotes.author: Proverb
quotes.security_relevance: Small, repeated security habits compound into stronger defense.
quotes.source_reference: Traditional Chinese proverb; no single author
quotes.translation_note: Proverb wording varies by collection.

quotes.text: Until the lions have their own historians, the history of the hunt will always glorify the hunter.
quotes.author: Proverb
quotes.security_relevance: Preserve evidence so the affected system has its own record.
quotes.source_reference: Traditional proverb; precise origin varies by collection
quotes.translation_note: Origin and wording vary; labeled as proverb, not a named-author quote.

quotes.text: Patience attracts happiness; it brings near that which is far.
quotes.author: Proverb
quotes.security_relevance: Patient triage helps avoid destructive or misleading response actions.
quotes.source_reference: Traditional Swahili proverb; no single author
quotes.translation_note: Proverb wording varies by collection.

quotes.text: Measure a thousand times and cut once.
quotes.author: Proverb
quotes.security_relevance: Validate evidence and impact before making irreversible changes.
quotes.source_reference: Traditional proverb; no single author
quotes.translation_note: Comparable forms exist in multiple cultures.

quotes.text: A small leak will sink a great ship.
quotes.author: Proverb
quotes.security_relevance: Small exposures can become large failures when ignored.
quotes.source_reference: Traditional proverb; no single author
quotes.translation_note: Comparable forms exist in multiple cultures.

quotes.text: A wise person changes their mind; a fool never will.
quotes.author: Proverb
quotes.security_relevance: Good security decisions change when evidence changes.
quotes.source_reference: Traditional Spanish proverb; no single author
quotes.translation_note: English rendering; wording varies.

quotes.text: Turn your face to the sun and the shadows fall behind you.
quotes.author: Proverb
quotes.security_relevance: Clear direction helps teams move through uncertainty.
quotes.source_reference: Traditional proverb often associated with Maori collections; no single author
quotes.translation_note: Wording varies; labeled as proverb.

quotes.text: Design systems so failure is visible, recoverable, and investigated.
quotes.author: Security Principle
quotes.security_relevance: Failures should create evidence and recovery paths instead of silent drift.
quotes.source_reference: Derived from CISA Secure by Design and NIST incident response guidance
quotes.translation_note: Paraphrased MSAA principle, not a direct agency quote.

quotes.text: Treat risk as context: identify assets, protect what matters, detect change, respond clearly, and recover deliberately.
quotes.author: Security Principle
quotes.security_relevance: Summarizes practical readiness across the security lifecycle.
quotes.source_reference: Derived from NIST CSF 2.0 Functions
quotes.translation_note: Paraphrased MSAA principle, not a direct NIST quote.

quotes.text: Grant only the access needed, only for the time needed, and only with evidence that it remains needed.
quotes.author: Security Principle
quotes.security_relevance: Access should be limited, reviewed, and reversible.
quotes.source_reference: Derived from NIST SP 800-53 Access Control concepts
quotes.translation_note: Paraphrased MSAA principle, not a direct NIST quote.

quotes.text: Assume one control can fail; build layers that slow, reveal, and contain the failure.
quotes.author: Security Principle
quotes.security_relevance: Layered controls make individual failures less catastrophic.
quotes.source_reference: Derived from NSA public hardening/readiness and NIST control concepts
quotes.translation_note: Paraphrased MSAA principle, not a direct NSA or NIST quote.

quotes.text: Preserve the timeline before changing the scene.
quotes.author: Security Principle
quotes.security_relevance: Evidence should be captured before remediation destroys context.
quotes.source_reference: Derived from NIST SP 800-61 incident response concepts
quotes.translation_note: Paraphrased MSAA principle, not a direct NIST quote.

quotes.text: Make the secure path the easy path, and make unsafe drift visible.
quotes.author: Security Principle
quotes.security_relevance: Defensive defaults should reduce avoidable mistakes and expose drift.
quotes.source_reference: Derived from CISA Secure by Design public guidance
quotes.translation_note: Paraphrased MSAA principle, not a direct CISA quote.

quotes.text: Control the tempo: make evidence, timing, and context work before you act.
quotes.author: MSAA
quotes.security_relevance: Encourages deliberate investigation before remediation.
quotes.source_reference: Original MSAA dashboard security culture entry

quotes.text: Power is easier to keep when your intentions are disciplined and your signals are deliberate.
quotes.author: MSAA
quotes.security_relevance: Disciplined operations reduce accidental exposure and noisy response.
quotes.source_reference: Original MSAA dashboard security culture entry

quotes.text: Influence starts with attention, but trust is won by restraint and precision.
quotes.author: MSAA
quotes.security_relevance: Security communication should be precise, restrained, and trust-building.
quotes.source_reference: Original MSAA dashboard security culture entry

quotes.text: Mastery comes from patient repetition, clear feedback, and ruthless correction of weak habits.
quotes.author: MSAA
quotes.security_relevance: Security maturity grows from repeated review and corrected weaknesses.
quotes.source_reference: Original MSAA dashboard security culture entry

quotes.text: Study the system until anomalies stand out without drama.
quotes.author: MSAA
quotes.security_relevance: Normal-baseline literacy improves anomaly review.
quotes.source_reference: Original MSAA dashboard security culture entry

quotes.text: Skill compounds when every investigation leaves better notes, cleaner tools, and sharper judgment.
quotes.author: MSAA
quotes.security_relevance: Good investigations improve future response capability.
quotes.source_reference: Original MSAA dashboard security culture entry
